title: Halting with a prescribed Boolean answer
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $o$ assign a Boolean answer to each of five oracle indices and each Boolean word. Let $st$ be a configuration of fifteen natural-number registers, each at most $B$, and let $q,p$ be Booleans with $q=p$. Starting with input $y$, register vector given by $st$, the answer state labeled true if and only if $q$ is true, and no recorded result, the abstract machine $A(a,b,f,m)$ halts with result $p$; at every earlier time its configuration satisfies the guard requiring its prescribed precondition and all register values to be at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: oracle $o$ on five indices and Boolean words
initial register configuration $st$ has every register at most $B$
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $o$ be an oracle on
five Boolean-word inputs, and let $y$ be a Boolean word. Suppose a state $st$ has all
fifteen register values at most $B$, and let $q,p$ be Booleans with $q=p$. The machine
$A(a,b,f,m)$, started on $y$ in the state labeled by the Boolean answer that is true
exactly when $q$ is true, with register vector $st$ and no recorded result, halts with
result $p$; at every earlier time its configuration satisfies the guard requiring the
prescribed precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
